items.title: Majority of Ontario fraud cases tossed since 2020 due to limited resources: Crowns’ association
items.description: CBC News reviewed the latest three years of fraud statistics released since its investigative series The Cost of Fraud revealed that only a fraction of fraud cases were making it through Ontario’s justice system a few years ago. The new numbers from Statistics Canada show the problem has only gotten worse, and have some experts pointing to alternative solutions to stem the flow of fraud.

items.title: Alberta lawyers must take Indigenous education course tied to TRC. New legislation could change that
items.description: A little more than five years ago, the regulator for Alberta's lawyers announced that moving forward, all active Alberta lawyers would be required to take a mandatory Indigenous education course. But new Alberta legislation could change that.

items.title: Ontario jails set to hit overcrowding record as bail reform looms, data shows
items.description: Ontario jails are heading toward a record year for overcrowding, remand populations and lockdowns just as politicians debate bail reforms that could lead to a further influx of accused behind bars, data analyzed by CBC News reveals.

items.title: Is Canada’s hockey culture broken?
items.description: Questioning hockey culture in Canada can be controversial, but it’s something award-winning author and sports journalist Rick Westhead doesn’t shy away from. In conversation with The National’s Ian Hanomansing, he lays out what he uncovered for his new book We Breed Lions and the impact he hopes it has on the sport.

items.title: Public warned to avoid B.C. resort over food, water and pool safety concerns
items.description: A resort in B.C.’s Interior is under a public health warning after inspectors found ongoing safety problems with its food, water and recreational facilities, issues officials say have persisted for years.

items.title: On Our Radar: Blue Jay Valley shows why East Van rules in video for "Living In the City"
items.description: The kids are more than alright.

items.title: Surrey police say a 9-year-old has died after collision with large vehicle
items.description: Surrey Police Service says in a statement released Sunday morning that the child died following a collision with what police say was a large cube van-style vehicle.

items.title: ANALYSIS: NDP leadership hopefuls reckon with oil and gas workers – and their votes
items.description: The federal NDP will select its new leader on March 29 and a key issue as they decide who to pick is how to develop -- or not develop -- the country's oil and gas resources.

items.title: We Fight Disinformation Every Day. You Can Help
items.description: The Tyee’s keeping it real with the support of our readers. And now we offer tax deduction receipts.

items.title: Emily Carr University Calls on the Next Generation of Creative Thinkers
items.description: Teens are invited to enter an art contest for a chance to win a scholarship to ECU’s summer teen programs.

items.title: How the BCGEU Strike Raised the Bar for Nurses and Teachers
items.description: The tense eight-month job action heightened expectations for other public sector workers seeking deals.

items.title: Fatal blaze in Fort William First Nation is 4th trailer fire in Thunder Bay, Ont., district in a week
items.description: Ontario’s Office of the Fire Marshal is investigating a fatal blaze in Fort William First Nation, which marks the fourth trailer fire in the Thunder Bay district within a week. Here's what we know about the recent incidents.

items.title: Montreal Victoire defeats Toronto Sceptres 3-1, land second straight win
items.description: Ann-Renée Desbiens made 21 saves, including 11 in the third period, as the Montreal Victoire defeated the Toronto Sceptres 3-1 in Professional Women's Hockey League action Sunday afternoon at Place Bell in Laval, Que.

items.title: Veterans Affairs demands repayment of some benefits; process shocks veterans' advocates
items.description: Veterans are receiving surprise letters demanding repayment of large benefit overpayments — debts advocates say may be caused by Veterans Affairs’ own errors.

items.description: The Nashville artist is touring in support of her new album, Blush.
